legend: This is an easier version of the next problem. In this version, q=0%%ZSMJ0%%.
A sequence of integers is called nice if its elements are arranged in blocks like in [3,3,3,4,1,1]%%ZSMJ1%%. Formally, if two elements are equal, everything in between must also be equal.

Let's define difficulty of a sequence as a minimum possible number of elements to change to get a nice sequence. However, if you change at least one element of value x%%ZSMJ2%% to value y%%ZSMJ3%%, you must also change all other elements of value x%%ZSMJ4%% into y%%ZSMJ5%% as well. For example, for [3,3,1,3,2,1,2]%%ZSMJ6%% it isn't allowed to change first 1%%ZSMJ7%% to 3%%ZSMJ8%% and second 1%%ZSMJ9%% to 2%%ZSMJ10%%. You need to leave 1%%ZSMJ11%%'s untouched or change them to the same value.
You are given a sequence of integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ12%% and q%%ZSMJ13%% updates.
Each update is of form "i%%ZSMJ14%% x%%ZSMJ15%%" — change ai%%ZSMJ16%% to x%%ZSMJ17%%. Updates are not independent (the change stays for the future).
Print the difficulty of the initial sequence and of the sequence after every update.
input: The first line contains integers n%%ZSMJ18%% and q%%ZSMJ19%% (1≤n≤200000%%ZSMJ20%%, q=0%%ZSMJ21%%), the length of the sequence and the number of the updates.
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ22%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ23%% (1≤ai≤200000%%ZSMJ24%%), the initial sequence.
Each of the following q%%ZSMJ25%% lines contains integers it%%ZSMJ26%% and xt%%ZSMJ27%% (1≤it≤n%%ZSMJ28%%, 1≤xt≤200000%%ZSMJ29%%), the position and the new value for this position.
output: Print q+1%%ZSMJ30%% integers, the answer for the initial sequence and the answer after every update.
